An unbranded plain red-brick storefront stands behind the crowd. No existing franchise character or real person. No fire, violence, weapons, real store name or numerical price claim.

Each paper rectangle is about300pixels wide and240pixels high, fully visible with all four corners and a generous air gap above every head. Both signs are front-facing and stay nearly stationary. Paper has absolutely no letters, numbers, drawings or symbols. Exactly two boards, no extra signs. No text anywhere else: storefront awning is a plain dark navy band, microphone is unlettered, computer and clothing unbranded. Exact enormous typography will be added in postproduction. A DIFFERENT pair of new original fictional adults in the same animated peaceful protest. Reporter screen-left: adult man with short dark curls, round dark glasses, plain mustard-yellow jacket, holding one black microphone in his right hand. Gamer screen-right: adult woman with wavy dark auburn shoulder-length hair and plain violet hoodie. A simple unbranded open laptop rests solidly on a table below y950, screen facing the woman, dark screen with no text. No SSD circuit board or tiny hand-held props. All objects stay with their owners and planted supports. These are new anthology interview characters, not the first take characters or recurring identities.
ACTING SCORE, a playful mock-eviction scene. The gamer wants the reporter to believe she manages her laptop like a strict apartment building. The reporter asks with genuine concern while looking at the laptop and then at her. She listens, adopts a mock-serious administrator posture and gives the first sentence with measured authority. Her voice becomes more emphatic and playful on the final clause without shouting or adding words. The reporter first processes the answer in a surprised blink and a quick glance at the laptop. Then he breaks professional composure into a loud, warm, genuine voiced laugh: he pulls the microphone away to his waist, tips his head back briefly, eyes narrow and shoulders bounce twice as he bends slightly forward. She is delighted that he understood, drops the administrator pose and answers with a short spontaneous laugh and a broad mischievous smile. One nearby supporter catches their laughter a moment later. Laughter ends naturally before the crowd slogan. The supporters then lift their chests and chant with spirited protest energy while both interviewees turn toward them and smile, mouths silent during the chant. Finish with relaxed breathing and an exchanged amused look. Do not turn every open mouth into laughter or make all bodies move together. The laptop stays on its table and the blank boards remain high, clear of hair and hands.
